question: How do I work with keys?

sections.title: What keys are and why Plantour uses them
items: A key in Plantour is a private saved credential record, such as an access token or another secret value that one feature may need.
Keys let you keep those values inside your own Plantour account instead of pasting them again every time you use the feature.
Plantour uses keys only when a certain workflow needs them. For example, private Dropbox images in trip notes need an active dropbox key.
This keeps optional integrations separate from your main trip data. If you do not use a feature that needs a key, you usually do not need to create one.

sections.title: Open the Keys dictionary
items: Plantour opens the Keys page where you can store private key records for your account.

sections.title: Add, update, or delete a key
sections.beforeHtml: Use keys when Plantour needs a saved token or private key value for a feature you want to use.
items: Click Add when you want to create a new key record.
Optionally keep the key Active and add notes that help you remember what it is for.
Select an existing key and use Update when you want to edit it, or Delete when you want to remove it.

sections.title: Use the active flag correctly
items: Plantour can use only keys that are marked as Active.
If a feature says that a key is missing, first check whether the correct key record exists and whether it is active.
Use the notes field when you want to record what service or scenario that key supports.

sections.title: Common example: Dropbox images in travel notes
items: The trip-notes Dropbox flow looks for an active key named dropbox.
When you want to insert private Dropbox images into notes, save your Dropbox access token in Keys and mark that key as active.
For the full Dropbox image workflow, continue with How do I keep travel notes?.
